summary: Reflections' cinematic open-world driving series, covering John Tanner's mainline games plus the portable and mobile spin-offs.

entries.title: Driver

emulation.emulator: Native PC compatibility / DuckStation for PS1
emulation.notes: Use PC compatibility fixes for the main route; use PS1 emulation only for console-original comparison.

primary.why: The Windows release is the highest-fidelity route for the original Driver and allows the Newcastle bonus area to be unlocked through normal play. The PlayStation original is historically central, but lower fidelity; GBC and mobile remakes are separate lower-fidelity adaptations.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version on a modern PC compatibility setup; use PlayStation/PSN only for original-console preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile versions are remakes/adaptations, not definitive replacements for the original PC/PlayStation game.

entries.title: Driver 2

emulation.notes: Use disc images from owned copies and enable higher internal resolution if desired.

primary.why: Driver 2's PlayStation version is the complete release with Chicago, Havana, Las Vegas, and Rio de Janeiro across two discs. Driver 2 Advance is significantly condensed to two cities and simplified story presentation, so it is not the main route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation discs on original hardware or DuckStation; use the GBA version only as a technical handheld adaptation.

entries.remaster_caveats: The GBA version is a condensed adaptation, not a replacement.

entries.title: Driver 3

emulation.emulator: Native PC compatibility / PCSX2 or xemu fallback
emulation.notes: Use PC for fidelity; fallback to PS2/Xbox emulation if compatibility issues block play.

primary.why: Driver 3 launched on PS2, Xbox, and mobile, then received a Windows port with enhanced graphics. Despite the PC version's critical reception, it is the highest-fidelity route for the full Miami/Nice/Istanbul game; GBA and mobile are separate lower-fidelity adaptations.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version with compatibility fixes; use PS2/Xbox only if PC compatibility is troublesome.

entries.remaster_caveats: Planned GameCube and N-Gage versions were canceled; PC needs compatibility care and was not well received technically.

entries.title: Driver: Vegas

emulation.notes: Use original mobile hardware or available mobile emulation.

primary.why: Driver: Vegas is a mobile-only, non-canon side game set after Driver 3. Mobile phone is the only sourced route.
primary.how_to_play: Use preserved compatible mobile hardware or a J2ME/BREW preservation setup where available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Non-canon mobile side game; preservation depends on old mobile platforms.

entries.title: Driver: Parallel Lines

emulation.emulator: Native PC compatibility / PCSX2 or xemu fallback
emulation.notes: Use Windows for the main route; fallback to sixth-generation console emulation if needed.

primary.why: Parallel Lines launched on PS2 and Xbox, then came to Windows and Wii in 2007. Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the full New York 1978/2006 game, while Wii has no sourced exclusive content advantage.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with compatibility fixes; use PS2/Xbox only for original-console comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Limited/collector editions include physical extras, not core-game content needed for the play route.

entries.title: Driver 76

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for higher internal resolution if desired.

primary.why: Driver 76 is a PSP-exclusive prequel to Driver: Parallel Lines, with its own mission structure, comic-style presentation, and ad hoc multiplayer. PSP is the sole platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PSP hardware, PlayStation TV where compatible, or PPSSPP.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or port is sourced.

entries.title: Driver: L.A. Undercover

emulation.notes: Use original mobile hardware or available mobile emulation.

primary.why: Driver: L.A. Undercover is a non-canon mobile side game released for BREW and J2ME. Those mobile versions are the only sourced route.
primary.how_to_play: Use preserved compatible mobile hardware or a J2ME/BREW preservation setup.

entries.remaster_caveats: Non-canon mobile side game; preservation depends on old mobile platforms.

entries.title: Driver: San Francisco
entries.definitive_edition: Windows main release plus Wii alternate-story supplement

emulation.emulator: Native PC / Dolphin for Wii supplement / RPCS3 or Xenia fallback
emulation.notes: Use PC for main route; use Dolphin for the Wii story route.

primary.why: The HD Driver: San Francisco release on PS3, Xbox 360, Windows, and Mac is the main sequel to Driver 3, and Windows provides the highest-fidelity route. The Wii release has a completely different story that acts as a prequel to the original Driver, so it is a secondary story route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release if already owned; preserve the Wii version separately for its alternate storyline.

secondary.exclusive_content: Completely different storyline acting as a prequel to the original Driver
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Wii campaign separately after the Windows main route.
secondary.why: It is lower fidelity but a distinct narrative version.

entries.remaster_caveats: The game has been delisted in many storefront contexts; play via legitimate existing copies.

entries.title: Driver: Renegade 3D

primary.why: Driver: Renegade 3D is a Nintendo 3DS-exclusive entry set between Driver and Driver 2. 3DS is the only sourced platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo 3DS hardware or a compatible 3DS preservation emulator.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or port is sourced.

entries.title: Driver: Speedboat Paradise

emulation.emulator: Original mobile hardware / Android preservation setup
emulation.notes: Use preserved installed copies where available.

primary.why: Speedboat Paradise is a free-to-play iOS/Android Driver spin-off built around speedboat missions rather than cars. iOS/Android are the only sourced platforms.
primary.how_to_play: Use a preserved installed copy on compatible iOS/Android hardware if available; expect live-service and delisting limitations.

entries.remaster_caveats: Free-to-play mobile/live-service preservation may be limited by delisting or server dependencies.
